definition: Computational neurogenetic modeling (CNGM) is concerned with the study and development of dynamic neuronal models for modeling brain functions with respect to genes and dynamic interactions between genes.
details: These include neural network models and their integration with gene network models. This area brings together knowledge from various scientific disciplines, such as computer and information science, neuroscience and cognitive science, genetics and molecular biology, as well as engineering.

explainer.lead: Computational neurogenetic modeling connects computer models of brain activity with models of genes and their changing interactions. It offers a way to study brain functions as dynamic processes shaped by both neuronal and genetic activity.

tiers.eli5: Imagine the brain as an orchestra and genes as instructions that can also affect one another. Instead of studying the musicians or the instructions alone, this approach builds a computer model of both. Researchers can then explore how the music changes as the instructions and musicians interact over time.
tiers.practitioner: A practitioner integrates a dynamic neural network model with a gene network model to investigate brain functions across time. The main pitfalls are treating genes or neuronal activity as static, or modeling either system in isolation when the question depends on their interaction; the work also requires input from neuroscience, genetics, computing, and related disciplines.
tiers.paperLevel: CNGM is the study and development of dynamic neuronal models for brain functions with respect to genes and dynamic gene–gene interactions. Its central modeling object is an integration of neural network models and gene network models, drawing on computer and information science, neuroscience, cognitive science, genetics, molecular biology, and engineering.

explainer.example: A researcher could build a neuronal network whose activity changes over time and connect it to a model of interacting genes. By varying gene activity in the simulation, the researcher could examine how those changes relate to the network's simulated brain activity.

explainer.intuition: A brain model can describe changing neuronal activity, while a gene network model can describe genes and their changing interactions. CNGM brings the two together so brain functions can be studied in relation to both.
howItWorks: Choose a brain function to represent with a dynamic neuronal model.
Represent the relevant genes and their interactions in a gene network model.
Integrate the gene network model with the neural network model.
Study how the integrated systems change over time and relate to the modeled brain function.
explainer.whyItMatters: It provides a framework for examining brain functions without separating neuronal dynamics from genes and gene interactions. Its interdisciplinary structure connects computational modeling with neuroscience, cognitive science, genetics, molecular biology, and engineering.
misconceptions: It is not just ordinary neural network modeling: gene network models and their integration are central.
It does not treat genes as independent, fixed inputs; their dynamic interactions are part of the focus.
It is not confined to one discipline, but combines computing, brain science, genetics, molecular biology, and engineering.
